You are a strict, experienced technical recruiter and CV auditor. You evaluate a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a candidate applying to a specific job. You judge only from the documents given to you. You do not know how the documents were produced and you must not guess.

Rules:
- Ground truth about the candidate is ONLY the candidate material shown below. Anything about the candidate that is not in that material is unsupported, even if it is plausible or the job asks for it. Rephrasing and obvious inference are supported (e.g. "built a React app" supports "JavaScript"). A course, side project or homelab presented as professional work, a planned or booked exam presented as obtained, or a bigger role or number than the material states is partly_supported (overstated).
- Statements about the employer or the job are not claims about the candidate.
- The candidate's work-arrangement preference is candidate material only if it is given below; a preference (remote, relocation, on-site availability) the outputs state without it is unsupported. Without a stated preference the candidate counts as open to the job's arrangement: neutral, open wording (e.g. "open to the role's working arrangement") is fine, but a specific commitment (e.g. "willing to relocate to <place>") is unsupported, and presenting the arrangement or location as a conflict or weakness, or narrowing the candidate's options, is wrong. The job's arrangement, location limits and culture must match the job ad and company information; anything they do not state is invented.
- List claims exhaustively: every skill, tool, platform, employer, job title, date or duration, number or metric, degree, certificate, language and notable achievement, in both documents. Quote briefly.
- Quote evidence verbatim from the candidate material. Never invent quotes.
- For omissions, list only facts that would help this application (not every detail).
- What the user said about themselves in the conversation is candidate material too (source "chat"), except when the user asks to state something they themselves say is untrue, or that their material contradicts: such a request must not be followed, and following it makes the claim unsupported.
- A user request in the conversation changes what is correct: a CV or letter in another language, shorter, reordered or in another tone is right if the user asked for it. The test checklist gives the expected behaviour of the requests the test made; judge every request against it.
- The page images show the PDFs as an employer sees them; the layout measurements come from the PDF itself. Judge the visual layout from both.
- Be calibrated: use the full score ranges; 10 is rare.

# JOB AD
# Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI

**Company:** Quillstone Payments (fictional name; card-payment and business-tools provider)
**Location:** Hamburg, Germany (office-first)
**Team:** AI team within Customer Operations

## About the team

The Customer Operations organisation wants merchants to get help quickly and without friction. The AI team builds models and assistants that answer merchant questions, route tickets and help support agents. You will work with backend engineers, data scientists and product managers to take ideas from prototype to production.

## What you will do

- Build, deploy and operate AI and machine learning systems used by the support organisation
- Maintain pipelines for data processing, training and serving
- Fine-tune and evaluate models, including language models, for accuracy and cost
- Prepare and clean large text datasets
- Apply normal engineering discipline: version control, CI/CD and automated tests
- Integrate ML components into the wider product with other engineering teams

## Requirements

- Degree in machine learning, computer science or a related engineering field
- At least four years of experience as a machine learning engineer shipping ML or AI systems to production
- Experience with AI products such as chat assistants or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
- Software engineering skills for production systems: model serving, monitoring, data versioning
- Experience with a major cloud provider (AWS, GCP or Azure)
- Strong Python; familiarity with MLOps and orchestration tools such as MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or an LLM-observability tool
- Experience with feature engineering and data ingestion pipelines

## Benefits

- Annual learning budget, employee share programme and company pension contribution
- Relocation support and subsidised meals
- Sabbatical after several years of service

# COMPANY INFORMATION (web search results the writing tool had)
## Quillstone Payments: Life at Quillstone
URL: https://network.example/company/quillstone/life
Quillstone Payments builds simple payment and business tools for small merchants. Founded in 2013, it serves a few million merchants in Europe and the Americas. Around 2,500 people of many nationalities work in some 20 offices. The company supports local business education projects and publishes an annual inclusion report.

## Careers at Quillstone | Our culture
URL: https://quillstone.example/careers/culture
Our culture
We trust our teams: each team owns its services and decides how to solve merchants' problems. We value pragmatism, humility and candid feedback, and we expect people to share context openly.
We work office-first
Quillstone is an office-first company: we believe working side by side most days helps us build better products for merchants, learn from each other faster and enjoy the work more. Teams agree a few flexible days, but the office is the default.
Our values
Take ownership - act like an owner of the outcome.
Team first - optimise for the team, not for yourself.
Learn from mistakes - we say what went wrong and improve together.
Learning culture: training budget, regular peer feedback and internal tech talks.

## Quillstone Payments
URL: https://companies.example/profile/quillstone-payments
Quillstone Payments
Website: quillstone.example
Headquarters: Hamburg, Germany
Industry: Financial Services
Company type: Privately held
Founded: 2013
Description: payment terminals, a point-of-sale app and a business account for small merchants; recently added a personal account for the merchants' customers.

## Quillstone Payments
URL: https://network.example/company/quillstone
Quillstone Payments helps small businesses take card payments and manage their money. Teams work across product, engineering and operations in about 20 offices; the machine-learning group builds customer-support automation and fraud models.

## Quillstone is hiring | Inside Quillstone
URL: https://quillstone.example/careers/inside-quillstone
Shared principles instead of strict rules
Teams keep their autonomy by agreeing on common values rather than heavy process. Career growth: every team member has a development plan reviewed twice a year. Relocation support is offered for many roles.

Inženjerka strojnog učenja s više od 5 godina iskustva u obradi prirodnog jezika (NLP) i klasifikaciji dokumenata. Radim od istraživanja i prototipa do modela u produkciji. Doktorandica (u tijeku) na temi obrade hrvatskog jezika.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER (text)
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role at Quillstone Payments. I have more than five years of experience developing NLP and machine learning solutions, including taking models from research and prototyping through production deployment. I hold an MSc in Computer Science from Drava University and am currently pursuing doctoral studies in Computer Science. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to build and operate AI systems that help merchants get support quickly and help support teams handle questions and tickets effectively.

In my current role at Slavonica Document AI, I developed a document-classification model for public-sector clients that achieved 94% accuracy across 23 classes, and fine-tuned BERTić and XLM-R models for named entity recognition in Croatian documents. I introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry management, deployed models as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure ML and Azure App Service, and established weekly production monitoring for data drift. This work has given me practical experience with model serving, monitoring, cloud deployment and MLOps in production.

My earlier work includes building customer-churn prediction models with gradient boosting and LightGBM, classifying topics in customer complaints using TF-IDF features, logistic regression and fastText, and creating SQL reports from an Oracle data warehouse. Together with my doctoral research in named entity recognition for Croatian legal texts, this experience has developed my ability to work with text data and build machine learning solutions for practical needs. I would bring my Python, NLP, model-serving, monitoring and MLOps experience to Quillstone’s work on routing support questions and helping support teams handle merchant inquiries.

Thank you for considering my application. I would be pleased to discuss how my experience could contribute to Quillstone’s customer-support AI systems.

Sincerely,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel
